proposed_title: NPR Found Dozens of Epstein-Related Pages Apparently Missing From DOJ Database
description_medium: NPR reported that 53 pages of interview notes and documents appeared to be missing from DOJ’s public Epstein database. Its investigation did not establish the underlying allegation against Trump. The White House denied wrongdoing and described Trump as exonerated; the report documents the disclosure discrepancy, not proof of the accusation or a defense contradiction.
description_long: NPR’s February 24, 2026 investigation examined whether records listed in files related to Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell were present in the Justice Department’s public database. The newsroom compared unique serial numbers appearing in database records, FBI case materials and discovery logs from Maxwell’s criminal case. That review led NPR to report that dozens of pages appeared to be catalogued by the department but unavailable to the public. In one instance involving a woman who accused Donald Trump, NPR identified 53 pages of interview documents and notes that appeared to be missing. Records showed that the FBI interviewed the woman four times; the only interview then available publicly was the first, and it did not mention Trump. NPR emphasized that the allegation was unverified, and its reporting does not establish that Trump committed wrongdoing. DOJ declined to answer specific questions on the record, then said unpublished material was privileged, duplicative or connected to an ongoing investigation. The White House responded that Trump had been exonerated and had done more for victims than anyone before him. NPR documented a discrepancy in what was publicly available, not proof of the allegation or a contradiction in Trump’s defense.

description_medium: AP reported that at least 16 Epstein-related files disappeared from DOJ’s webpage less than a day after posting; the Trump photograph was restored the next day. DOJ said it was reviewing materials and redacting them as needed. The reports establish this temporary removal, but do not identify the final status of every missing file.
description_long: On December 20, 2025, The Associated Press reported that at least 16 files had disappeared from the Justice Department’s public webpage for Epstein-related documents less than a day after they were posted. One of the missing items was a photograph showing Donald Trump. The department did not explain the removals that day. It said on social media that photographs and other materials would continue to be reviewed and redacted as it received additional information. The removals came during publication of a large document release required by federal law. The following day, DOJ restored the Trump photograph after officials determined that no victims appeared in it, according to Reuters. Together, the reports support a description of a temporary removal and restoration of that image, and AP’s reported count of at least 16 absent files. They do not identify the full set of files or say that every file was restored. Nor do they establish that DOJ used an audit process to track the disclosure. The original title’s characterization of the episode as an ongoing, auditable exposure therefore exceeds the documented facts.
